author: Fan Chen
description:
Vuk Jeremic is a former Serbian foreign minister and served as president of the United Nations General Assembly from 2012 to 2013. He was also a candidate for UN secretary general in 2016, finishing in second place behind Antonio Guterres. Jeremic now heads the Centre for International Relations and Sustainable Development, a think tank based in Serbia.
In this Open Questions interview, Jeremic discusses Europe’s geopolitical standing, transatlantic ties and China-Europe relations. He also...
title: Serbia’s ex-foreign minister Vuk Jeremic on China’s rise in a ‘geopolitical recession’

author: Zhou Bo
description:
Is a trilateral summit between China, Russia and the United States possible during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen? If so, it is striking that US President Donald Trump sees such a meeting focusing less on Ukraine, saying: “we would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearisation.”
How might this start? The US says China is the fastest-growing nuclear power in recent years. But even if Beijing’s warhead stockpile reached 600 by the end of 2025, as estimated by...
title: 5 steps China, US and Russia could take at Apec to defuse nuclear risk

author: Nayan Seth,Amber Wang
description:
The United States and China are working to iron out a military accident-prevention agreement ahead of their summit in Shenzhen, although progress has been slow amid divisions within the US administration, according to sources.
Both sides were still trying to reach common ground on a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on military-related crisis communication and prevention, sources said on condition of anonymity as they were not authorised to speak on the matter publicly.
The MOU was first...
title: US, China seek common ground on military crisis pact as Washington weighs terms: sources

author: Amber Wang
description:
New state media footage has surfaced showing for the first time what appears to be a Chinese-modified variant of the Russian-origin Kh-29T air-to-surface missile mounted on a J-10C fighter jet.
State broadcaster CCTV’s social media account posted a video on Wednesday featuring Chinese fighters, showing the missile mounted under the 4.5-generation fighter as it took off, according to posts by Chinese military bloggers over the weekend.
China originally imported about 2,000 Kh-29T missiles...
title: Chinese J-10C fighter spotted carrying modified Russian-origin heavy-strike missile

author: Chao Kong
description:
Science prizes usually put the spotlight on winners, celebrating their discoveries but paying little attention to the researchers left out.
A study by scientists at the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) has found that prominent innovation awards may discourage colleagues from pursuing unconventional research – with the most prestigious prizes having the strongest negative effect.
The findings raise questions about the wider consequences of scientific honours, including the Nobel Prize, as...
title: More Nobel winners, less innovation? Chinese study reveals cost of top-tier awards

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
China and Southeast Asian nations have made progress in negotiating a code of conduct for the South China Sea, with Manila announcing that roughly 80 per cent of the draft agreement is complete.
Yet whether the long-awaited accord can meet its year-end deadline comes down to Beijing and regional claimants finding common ground on key concessions, according to a Chinese expert.
Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro said on Saturday after a series of Asean ministerial meetings that 77 per...
title: South China Sea code of conduct: can Beijing and Asean meet 2026 deadline?

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Genetic diversity is nature’s insurance policy – an evolutionary safety net that provides the building blocks for natural selection.
While members of the same species share a mostly identical genome, a sliver of unique genetic variants determines their individual traits. When this diversity erodes, and a population becomes more uniform, it could leave them vulnerable to the same threats and unable to adapt when new ones emerge.
In China, scientists have found that common songbird species were...
title: Evolutionary threat: Chinese mountain birds lost nearly half genetic diversity in 50 years

author: Holly Chik
description:
Chinese ambassador to the United States Xie Feng has signalled high hopes for major-power cooperation at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen this week, promoting a China-led AI alliance for regional prosperity.
The prosperity theme was also highlighted in Qiushi, the Communist Party’s flagship publication, which compiled a series of President Xi Jinping’s previous Apec speeches on building an “Asia-Pacific community with a shared future”.
Since his first Apec meeting...
title: China calls for AI cooperation with the US ahead of Shenzhen Apec summit

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China has upgraded its VT-4 series main battle tank with cutting-edge technologies aimed at the international market, newly surfaced photos show ahead of the country’s premier defence exhibition in Zhuhai.
The appearance of the new tank, believed to be designated as VT-4B, indicates significant upgrades over the existing VT-4A in its armour protection, active protection, weapon station and electronic equipment.
Some of the improvements show traits of technologies developed for China’s...
title: China’s upgraded VT-4B export tank gets fourth-gen Type 100 tech ahead of Zhuhai show

author: Caroline Lin
description:
China’s bricks-and-mortar bookstores are increasingly counting on coffee, merchandise and cultural events rather than books to stay afloat – a survival strategy whose tensions were laid bare after a major chain asked a book buyer to vacate its cafe seating unless she bought a drink.
The dispute at a Beijing branch of Sisyphe Bookstore, one of the country’s largest chains, went viral earlier this month, sparking an online debate over the struggles bookshops face in the digital age.
The customer,...
title: What a Beijing cafe dispute reveals about China’s struggling bookshops

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Before mainland Chinese troops could attempt a landing on Taiwan, they would first have to assemble vehicles, weapons and supplies along the coast – potentially exposing them to Taiwanese drone, rocket and missile attacks.
A nighttime drill reported by state broadcaster CCTV on June 11 offered a glimpse of how the People’s Liberation Army could shield those amphibious forces as they prepared to cross the Taiwan Strait.
As soldiers headed into open water aboard amphibious armoured vehicles, a...
title: Could Beijing’s HQ-17 air-defence system defend PLA amphibious forces from Taiwan strikes?

author: Alcott Wei
description:
Pseudo-history about China is mushrooming online, spreading fake accounts of the past due in large part to platform algorithms, artificial intelligence (AI) and a lack of monitoring, according to a Chinese provincial authority.
In a commentary published on Monday, “Zhejiang Propaganda” – a social media account affiliated with the propaganda department of the province’s Communist Party committee – said the “pseudo-historical school” was gaining ground online, resurfacing despite crackdowns and...
title: Chinese social media firms under fire as fake history spreads online
